title: After dropping bank witnesses, Duterte defense seeks trade, FDA records
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team is seeking four new witnesses for her impeachment trial, including an anti-money laundering lawyer and officials from DTI, FDA and CITEM.

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte's lead defense counsel Shiela Sison reacts during a manifestation at the impeachment trial on Nov. 10, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — After dropping all 16 bank officials from its witness list, Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team is seeking to summon an anti-money laundering lawyer and three government officials to testify on financial regulations and records involving Cale88 Foods Corp. in her impeachment trial.
In a manifestation dated November 13, the defense asked the Senate impeachment court to issue subpoenas for four witnesses it intends to present during the November 19 and 20 hearings.

The witnesses are being sought in connection with Article II of the articles of impeachment, which covers allegations involving Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) and alleged ill-gotten wealth.
The first proposed witness is Rainer Dela Fuente, a lawyer from AML Consulting PH, whom the defense wants to testify on fundamental legal concepts under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

The defense also sought subpoenas for three officials from the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Center for International Expositions and Missions (CITEM).
The officials are being asked to testify and produce certified true copies of government records involving Cale88 Foods Corporation.

items: Ceferino Rodolfo, DTI undersecretary and Board of Investments managing head, who is being asked to testify on Cale88's BOI registration and submit its registration documents, certificate of registration and related correspondence.

Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan, director IV of the FDA's Center for Food Regulation and Research, who is being asked to testify on the company's registration of its sweetened banana chips product and produce its registration filings and Certificate of Product Registration.

Rowena Mendoza, department manager III at CITEM, or another authorized CITEM representative, who is being asked to testify on communications and invitations sent to Cale88 concerning food expositions. The defense also seeks correspondence between the company and DTI or CITEM.

blocks.text: The request follows the defense's withdrawal of all 16 bank officials it had previously listed as witnesses in the impeachment trial.
On November 12, the defense dropped 15 bank representatives from its witness list, initially retaining only Bank of the Philippine Islands senior vice president Paul Roderick Ysmael.
The following day, the defense also withdrew Ysmael, leaving none of the 16 bank officials to testify.
